name: Mathematics (A-Level: Pure Mathematics, Statistics, Mechanics / AS & A Level Mathematics)

concepts.name: Indices and variation
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only: ZIMSEC Pure (F5, Indices and proportionality); assumed knowledge for Cambridge. The laws of indices with zero, negative and rational indices, simplifying numerical and algebraic expressions, and equations in indices solved by writing both sides as powers of one base or by a substitution giving a quadratic in aˣ. Direct, inverse, joint and partial variation: forming the equation with a constant of proportionality, finding the constant from data and using the model (including life problems). Equations that need logarithms are in amaths.functions.logarithms.

concepts.name: Polynomials: division, identities, and the factor and remainder theorems
concepts.description: ZIMSEC Pure (F5) and Cambridge P2 (AS only) and P3 (A Level only), topics 2.1 / 3.1. Adding, subtracting and multiplying polynomials; long division of a polynomial of degree up to 4 by a linear or quadratic polynomial, giving quotient and remainder (which may be zero); identities versus equations and finding unknown coefficients by equating coefficients or substituting values (named by ZIMSEC); the remainder theorem (remainder f(−b/a) on division by ax + b) and the factor theorem, factorising cubics and quartics, solving polynomial equations and finding unknown coefficients from given factors or remainders.

concepts.name: Partial fractions
concepts.description: ZIMSEC Pure (F5) and Cambridge P3 (A Level only), topic 3.1. Decomposing proper rational functions with denominators (ax + b)(cx + d)(ex + f), (ax + b)(cx + d)² and (ax + b)(cx² + d) by substitution and by equating coefficients. ZIMSEC also includes improper fractions (divide first so that the numerator's degree is below the denominator's); Cambridge excludes them. Using partial fractions in series and integration is practised in amaths.series.binomial-rational and amaths.integ.partial-fractions.

concepts.name: The modulus function: graphs, equations and inequalities
concepts.description: ZIMSEC Pure (F5, absolute value and modulus functions) and Cambridge P2 (AS only) and P3 (A Level only). The meaning of |x|; sketching y = |ax + b|; the relations |a| = |b| ⇔ a² = b² and |x − a| < b ⇔ a − b < x < a + b; solving equations and inequalities such as |3x − 2| = |2x + 7| and 2x + 5 < |x + 1| algebraically and graphically. Graphs of y = |f(x)| for non-linear f are ZIMSEC only and are in amaths.functions.transformations.

concepts.name: Completing the square and the discriminant
concepts.description: ZIMSEC Pure (F5) and Cambridge P1 (AS & A Level), topic 1.1. Writing ax² + bx + c in completed-square form; the vertex, line of symmetry, maximum or minimum value and range of a quadratic; sketching the graph; the discriminant b² − 4ac and the number of real roots (two, one repeated root, none); finding the set of values of k for which an equation has real roots, or for which a line meets, touches or misses a curve (y = x + k and a quadratic curve).

concepts.name: Quadratic equations, inequalities and simultaneous equations
concepts.description: ZIMSEC Pure (F5) and Cambridge P1 (AS & A Level), topic 1.1. Solving quadratic equations by factorising, completing the square and the formula; quadratic inequalities with a sketch or sign table; simultaneous equations with one linear and one quadratic equation by substitution; equations that are quadratic in a function of x (x⁴ − 5x² + 4 = 0, 6x + √x − 1 = 0, tan²x = 1 + tan x), rejecting impossible values. ZIMSEC only: cubic and rational inequalities (for example (x − 1)/(x + 2) > 3) solved with critical values and sign tables, and modelling situations with equations and inequalities.

concepts.name: Matrices: operations, determinants, inverses and linear systems
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only: ZIMSEC Pure (F6, Matrices). Types of matrix (null, identity, square, singular, non-singular); adding, subtracting and multiplying matrices up to 3 × 3 and conformability; determinants of 2 × 2 and 3 × 3 matrices; the inverse of a non-singular 2 × 2 and 3 × 3 matrix (cofactors / adjoint); (AB)⁻¹ = B⁻¹A⁻¹; writing two or three simultaneous linear equations as AX = b and solving them with the inverse, with a word on inconsistent systems and systems with infinitely many solutions when the determinant is zero.

concepts.name: Matrices and transformations of the plane
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only: ZIMSEC Pure (F6, Matrices). 2 × 2 matrices representing enlargements and rotations about the origin, reflections in lines through the origin, stretches parallel to an axis and shears; finding the matrix from the images of the unit vectors; images of points, lines and shapes; composite transformations AB (B first) and powers Aⁿ; inverse transformations; the area scale factor of a transformation equals |det A| (derived and used).

concepts.name: Proof by mathematical induction
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only: ZIMSEC Pure (F6, Mathematical induction). The structure of an induction proof (basis, inductive hypothesis, inductive step, conclusion) and why it works; proving summation formulas, divisibility results, formulas for powers of matrices and nth terms of recurrence relations; conducting limited trials to form a conjecture and then proving it by induction. Written proofs are self-marked against mark-scheme points.

concepts.name: Binary operations and groups
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only: ZIMSEC Pure (F6, Groups). Binary operations on a set and Cayley tables; closure, commutativity, associativity, distributivity, identity element and inverse elements; the definition of a group; showing that a given structure (integers under addition, residues modulo n under addition or multiplication, symmetries, sets of matrices or functions under composition) is or is not a group; solving simple problems on binary operations and group properties. Subgroups, Lagrange's theorem and isomorphism are not named in the syllabus and are excluded.

concepts.name: Functions and relations: mappings, domain and range
concepts.description: ZIMSEC Pure (F5, Relations) and Cambridge P1 (AS & A Level), topic 1.2. Function, domain and range; one-one functions; finding the range of a given function in simple cases (for example 1/x for x ≥ 1, x² + 1 for real x); deciding whether a function is one-one. ZIMSEC only: relations and types of relation, co-domain, and the terms injective, surjective and bijective.

concepts.name: Composite and inverse functions
concepts.description: ZIMSEC Pure (F5) and Cambridge P1 (AS & A Level), topic 1.2. Forming composite functions fg and gf, the condition that gf exists only when the range of f lies within the domain of g; finding the inverse of a one-one function (including after completing the square, such as (2x + 3)² − 4 for x < −3/2); restricting a domain so that an inverse exists; the graphs of a function and its inverse as reflections in y = x.

concepts.name: Transformations of graphs
concepts.description: ZIMSEC Pure (F5) and Cambridge P1 (AS & A Level), topic 1.2. The graphs of y = f(x) + a, y = f(x + a), y = af(x), y = f(ax) and simple combinations, described with the words translation, reflection and stretch (with the vector, the line or the scale factor and direction); applied to algebraic and trigonometric functions or graphs given by their features. ZIMSEC only: the relationship between y = f(x) and y = |f(x)| for any f.

concepts.name: Exponential and logarithmic functions: eˣ and ln x
concepts.description: ZIMSEC Pure (F5) and Cambridge P2 (AS only) and P3 (A Level only), topics 2.2 / 3.2. The definition and properties of eˣ and ln x, their relationship as inverse functions and their graphs (including y = e^(kx) for positive and negative k, y = ln(ax + b)); exponential growth and decay in context (populations, cooling, depreciation, radioactive decay), finding constants and interpreting them.

concepts.name: Laws of logarithms; equations and inequalities with unknown indices
concepts.description: ZIMSEC Pure (F5) and Cambridge P2 (AS only) and P3 (A Level only). The relationship between logarithms and indices; the laws of logarithms (Cambridge excludes change of base; ZIMSEC does not say); solving equations aˣ = b and inequalities aˣ < b with logarithms (2ˣ < 5, 3 × 2^(3x−1) < 5, 3^(x+1) = 4^(2x−1)), logarithmic equations, exact and 3-significant-figure answers.

concepts.name: Reducing relationships to linear form
concepts.description: ZIMSEC Pure (F5) and Cambridge P2 (AS only) and P3 (A Level only). Using logarithms to transform y = kxⁿ (ln y against ln x) and y = k(aˣ) (ln y against x) to a straight line, and ZIMSEC's other linear forms such as y = ax² + b with y plotted against x²; finding the unknown constants from the gradient and intercept of a given line or of a line drawn from data.

concepts.name: Curve sketching and graphical solution of equations
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only: ZIMSEC Pure (F5, Graphs and coordinate geometry); assumed knowledge for Cambridge. Sketching y = kxⁿ (n an integer or ½), quadratic and cubic polynomials and simple rational functions with intercepts, turning points and asymptotes; using sketches to locate the solutions of equations and inequalities and to count roots.

concepts.name: Coordinate geometry of straight lines
concepts.description: ZIMSEC Pure (F5) and Cambridge P1 (AS & A Level), topic 1.3. Finding the equation of a line from two points or a point and a gradient; the forms y = mx + c, y − y₁ = m(x − x₁) and ax + by + c = 0; distances, midpoints, gradients, intersections; parallel and perpendicular lines and perpendicular bisectors; the link between points of intersection of graphs and solutions of equations. ZIMSEC only: the perpendicular distance from a point to a line.

concepts.name: The equation of a circle
concepts.description: ZIMSEC Pure (F5) and Cambridge P1 (AS & A Level), topic 1.3. (x − a)² + (y − b)² = r² and the expanded form x² + y² + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0, centre and radius; elementary circle geometry (tangent perpendicular to radius, angle in a semicircle, symmetry); finding a circle through given points; intersections of lines and circles, tangents, and the values of k for which a line meets, touches or misses a circle. Implicit differentiation is not used here.

concepts.name: Radians, arcs, sectors and segments
concepts.description: ZIMSEC Pure (F5, Plane trigonometry) and Cambridge P1 (AS & A Level), topic 1.4. The radian and conversion to and from degrees; arc length s = rθ and sector area ½r²θ; segment areas, perimeters, and lengths, angles and areas of triangles in compound shapes. ZIMSEC only: small-angle approximations sin x ≈ x, tan x ≈ x, cos x ≈ 1 − x²/2.

concepts.name: Trigonometric graphs, exact values and inverse trigonometric functions
concepts.description: ZIMSEC Pure (F5) and Cambridge P1 (AS & A Level), topic 1.5. Graphs of sine, cosine and tangent for any angle in degrees or radians and their transformations (y = 3 sin x, y = 1 − cos 2x, y = tan(x + π/4)); exact values for 30°, 45°, 60° and related angles; sin⁻¹x, cos⁻¹x, tan⁻¹x as principal values. ZIMSEC only: sketching (and transforming) the graphs of the inverse trigonometric relations.

concepts.name: Basic trigonometric identities and equations
concepts.description: ZIMSEC Pure (F5) and Cambridge P1 (AS & A Level), topic 1.5. tan θ ≡ sin θ / cos θ and sin²θ + cos²θ ≡ 1 to prove identities, simplify expressions and solve equations; finding all solutions of simple trigonometric equations in a given interval (3 sin 2x + 1 = 0 for −π < x < π, 3 sin²θ − 5 cos θ − 1 = 0 for 0° ≤ θ ≤ 360°). General solutions are not required (Cambridge).

concepts.name: Secant, cosecant and cotangent
concepts.description: ZIMSEC Pure (F5) and Cambridge P2 (AS only) and P3 (A Level only), topics 2.3 / 3.3. The relationship of sec, cosec and cot to cos, sin and tan; their properties and graphs for any angle; sec²θ ≡ 1 + tan²θ and cosec²θ ≡ 1 + cot²θ in proofs, simplification and equations (tan θ + cot θ = 4, 2 sec²θ − tan θ = 5).

concepts.name: Compound-angle and double-angle formulae
concepts.description: ZIMSEC Pure (F5) and Cambridge P2 (AS only) and P3 (A Level only). sin(A ± B), cos(A ± B), tan(A ± B); sin 2A, cos 2A (three forms) and tan 2A; exact values, simplification (cos(x − 30°) − 3 sin(x − 60°)), proofs and equations. ZIMSEC excludes half-angle identities (the t = tan ½θ formulae).

concepts.name: Expressing a sin θ + b cos θ as R sin(θ ± α) or R cos(θ ± α)
concepts.description: Cambridge P2 (AS only) and P3 (A Level only); ZIMSEC Pure (F5) teaches it within trigonometrical identities (not named in the document; confirm). Finding R and α, using the form to solve equations such as 3 cos θ + 2 sin θ = 1, and to find maximum and minimum values and where they occur.

concepts.name: Sequences, sigma notation and arithmetic progressions
concepts.description: ZIMSEC Pure (F5) and Cambridge P1 (AS & A Level), topic 1.6. Sequences defined by a formula or a recurrence (uₙ = n², uₙ₊₁ = 2uₙ); Σ notation; arithmetic progressions: nth term, sum of the first n terms, a, b, c in arithmetic progression when 2b = a + c, problems in context. ZIMSEC only: periodic, oscillating, convergent and divergent sequences.

concepts.name: Geometric progressions and the sum to infinity
concepts.description: ZIMSEC Pure (F5) and Cambridge P1 (AS & A Level), topic 1.6. nth term and sum of a geometric progression; a, b, c in geometric progression when b² = ac; the condition |r| < 1 for convergence and the sum to infinity; questions involving more than one progression (an arithmetic and a geometric progression sharing terms).

concepts.name: The binomial expansion for a positive integer index
concepts.description: ZIMSEC Pure (F5) and Cambridge P1 (AS & A Level), topic 1.6. Expanding (a + b)ⁿ for positive integer n with the notations n! and nCr (written as a bracketed binomial coefficient); finding a given term, coefficient or the term independent of x; expansions of products such as (1 + 2x)(3 − x)⁵. The greatest term and properties of the coefficients are not required.

concepts.name: The binomial expansion for a rational index
concepts.description: ZIMSEC Pure (F5) and Cambridge P3 (A Level only), topic 3.1. Expanding (1 + x)ⁿ for rational n and |x| < 1; adapting to (a + bx)ⁿ such as (2 − ½x)⁻¹ and stating the set of values of x for which the expansion is valid; expansions of rational functions after splitting into partial fractions; approximations. Finding the general term is not included (Cambridge).

concepts.name: Standard sums and the method of differences
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only: ZIMSEC Pure (F6, Series). The standard results for Σr, Σr² and Σr³ and their use to find related sums (Σ r(r + 1), sums from r = n + 1 to 2n); the method of differences (often after partial fractions) to sum a finite series and, where it converges, to find the sum to infinity.

concepts.name: Maclaurin and Taylor series
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only: ZIMSEC Pure (F6, Series). Maclaurin series by repeated differentiation; the standard series for eˣ, sin x, cos x, ln(1 + x) and (1 + x)ⁿ with their ranges of validity; series of products and composites; Taylor series about x = a; using series for approximation.

concepts.name: The gradient of a curve and differentiation from first principles
concepts.description: ZIMSEC Pure (F5) and Cambridge P1 (AS & A Level), topic 1.7. The gradient at a point as the limit of the gradients of chords (for example between x = 2 and x = 2 + h on y = x³), and the notations dy/dx, f′(x), d²y/dx², f″(x). Cambridge needs only the informal idea; ZIMSEC asks for differentiation from first principles of polynomials, rational functions and sine and cosine (not exponential or logarithmic functions).

concepts.name: Differentiating powers of x and the chain rule
concepts.description: ZIMSEC Pure (F5) and Cambridge P1 (AS & A Level), topic 1.7. The derivative of xⁿ for any rational n with constant multiples, sums and differences; composite functions by the chain rule (√(2x³ + 5), (3 − 2x)⁻⁴); second derivatives.

concepts.name: Tangents, normals, increasing functions and rates of change
concepts.description: ZIMSEC Pure (F5) and Cambridge P1 (AS & A Level), topic 1.7. Gradients, equations of tangents and normals, increasing and decreasing functions, rates of change and connected rates of change (given the rate of increase of a radius, find the rate of increase of an area or volume at an instant).

concepts.name: Stationary points, optimisation and curve sketching
concepts.description: ZIMSEC Pure (F5) and Cambridge P1 (AS & A Level), topic 1.7. Locating stationary points and determining their nature by the second derivative or by the change of sign of dy/dx; using stationary points to sketch graphs; practical maximum and minimum problems. ZIMSEC only: points of inflexion (Cambridge excludes them).

concepts.name: Derivatives of exponential, logarithmic and trigonometric functions
concepts.description: ZIMSEC Pure (F5) and Cambridge P2 (AS only) and P3 (A Level only), topics 2.4 / 3.4. Derivatives of eˣ, ln x, sin x, cos x and tan x with constant multiples, sums, differences and composites (e^(1−x²), ln(3x + 2), sin²3x). A Level only (Cambridge P3): the derivative of tan⁻¹x (sin⁻¹x and cos⁻¹x not required); ZIMSEC does not name inverse trigonometric derivatives (confirm).

concepts.name: The product and quotient rules
concepts.description: ZIMSEC Pure (F5) and Cambridge P2 (AS only) and P3 (A Level only). Differentiating products and quotients ((2x − 4)/(3x + 2), x² ln x, x e^(1−x²)), simplifying the result and using it for gradients, tangents, normals and stationary points.

concepts.name: Implicit and parametric differentiation
concepts.description: ZIMSEC Pure (F5) and Cambridge P2 (AS only) and P3 (A Level only). The first derivative of a curve defined implicitly (x² + y² = xy + 7) or parametrically (x = t − e^(2t), y = t + e^(2t)), with tangents and normals. ZIMSEC also asks learners to define a curve by parametric equations and convert to a Cartesian equation (Form 5 coordinate geometry); that is taught here.

concepts.name: Integration as the reverse of differentiation
concepts.description: ZIMSEC Pure (F5) and Cambridge P1 (AS & A Level), topic 1.8. Integrating (ax + b)ⁿ for rational n ≠ −1 with constant multiples, sums and differences; the constant of integration; finding the equation of a curve from dy/dx and a point.

concepts.name: Definite integrals and areas
concepts.description: ZIMSEC Pure (F5) and Cambridge P1 (AS & A Level), topic 1.8. Evaluating definite integrals including simple improper integrals (∫₀¹ x^(−1/2) dx, ∫₁^∞ x⁻² dx); the area of a region bounded by a curve and lines parallel to the axes, between a curve and a line, and between two curves, with regions below the x-axis handled correctly.

concepts.name: Volumes of revolution
concepts.description: ZIMSEC Pure (F5) and Cambridge P1 (AS & A Level), topic 1.8. Volumes generated by rotating a region through 360° about the x-axis or the y-axis, including regions not bounded by the axis of rotation (between y = 9 − x² and y = 5); exact answers in terms of π. At A Level the integrands may use any technique of the family.

concepts.name: Integrating exponential, reciprocal and trigonometric functions
concepts.description: ZIMSEC Pure (F5) and Cambridge P2 (AS only) and P3 (A Level only), topics 2.5 / 3.5. Integrating e^(ax+b), 1/(ax + b), sin(ax + b), cos(ax + b) and sec²(ax + b); using trigonometric identities to integrate sin²x, cos²2x and tan²x. A Level only (Cambridge P3; ZIMSEC standard integrals): 1/(x² + a²) = (1/a) tan⁻¹(x/a), e.g. 1/(2 + 3x²).

concepts.name: Integration by recognition and by substitution
concepts.description: ZIMSEC Pure (F5) and Cambridge P3 (A Level only), topic 3.5. Recognising integrands of the form k f′(x)/f(x) (x/(x² + 1), tan x) and f′(x)[f(x)]ⁿ and integrating them; using a given substitution (Cambridge) or a suitable substitution (ZIMSEC) to evaluate definite and indefinite integrals, changing the limits (sin²2x cos x with u = sin x).

concepts.name: Integration using partial fractions
concepts.description: ZIMSEC Pure (F5) and Cambridge P3 (A Level only), topic 3.5. Integrating rational functions after decomposition into the partial-fraction types of amaths.algebra.partial-fractions, giving answers with ln terms combined, and exact definite integrals (ZIMSEC: improper fractions too).

concepts.name: Integration by parts
concepts.description: ZIMSEC Pure (F5) and Cambridge P3 (A Level only), topic 3.5. Recognising when an integrand is a product and using integration by parts (x sin 2x, x²e⁻ˣ, ln x, x tan⁻¹x), repeated application, definite integrals by parts. Also used for the exponential distribution in ZIMSEC Statistics.

concepts.name: Locating roots and iterative methods
concepts.description: ZIMSEC Pure (F6) and Cambridge P2 (AS only) and P3 (A Level only), topics 2.6 / 3.6. Locating a root by graphical considerations or a change of sign (between consecutive integers); sequences of approximations converging to a root; how an iteration xₙ₊₁ = F(xₙ) relates to the equation, using a given iteration or rearrangement to find a root to a stated accuracy; an iteration may fail to converge. ZIMSEC also asks learners to derive a converging iterative formula (Cambridge does not require the convergence condition).

concepts.name: The Newton–Raphson method
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only: ZIMSEC Pure (F6, Numerical methods). Deriving the Newton–Raphson formula xₙ₊₁ = xₙ − f(xₙ)/f′(xₙ) from the tangent, applying it to a stated accuracy, and recognising when it fails or converges to an unwanted root (poor starting value, f′ near zero).

concepts.name: The trapezium rule and numerical errors
concepts.description: ZIMSEC Pure (F6) and Cambridge P2 (AS only; topic 2.5, not in P3). The trapezium rule to estimate a definite integral, and using a sketch (concavity) to decide whether it over- or under-estimates. ZIMSEC only: deriving the rule, bounds for an area using rectangles or trapezia, and errors (absolute and relative error, estimating errors in calculations).

concepts.name: Vectors in two and three dimensions
concepts.description: ZIMSEC Pure (F5), ZIMSEC Mechanics (F5, Vectors) and Cambridge P3 (A Level only), topic 3.7. Notation (column vectors, xi + yj + zk, AB with an arrow, bold a); position, displacement, free and unit vectors; magnitude; addition, subtraction and scalar multiplication with geometric meaning (OABC a parallelogram ⇔ OB = OA + OC, midpoint ½(OA + OB)); parallel vectors. ZIMSEC Mechanics also: the triangle law, resolving a vector into components and finding resultants.

concepts.name: The scalar product
concepts.description: ZIMSEC Pure (F5) and Cambridge P3 (A Level only), topic 3.7. a · b = |a||b| cos θ and the component formula; the angle between two vectors; perpendicular vectors; problems on 3-D objects (cuboids, pyramids/tetrahedra). The vector product is ZIMSEC only (amaths.vectors.cross-product-planes).

concepts.name: Vector equations of lines
concepts.description: ZIMSEC Pure (F6) and Cambridge P3 (A Level only), topic 3.7. The line r = a + tb and the meaning of each symbol; the equation from a point and a direction or from two points; deciding whether two lines are parallel, intersect or are skew, and finding the point of intersection; the angle between two lines; the foot of the perpendicular from a point to a line and the perpendicular distance. ZIMSEC only: Cartesian equations of a line in three dimensions. The shortest distance between skew lines is excluded.

concepts.name: The vector product and equations of planes
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only: ZIMSEC Pure (F6). The vector (cross) product, its properties and use to find areas of triangles and parallelograms and normal vectors; vector, parametric and Cartesian equations of a plane (r · n = d, ax + by + cz = d) from a point and a normal, from three points, or from a point and two directions.

concepts.name: Lines and planes: angles, intersections and distances
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only: ZIMSEC Pure (F6). The angle between a line and a plane and between two planes; whether a line lies in, is parallel to or meets a plane, and the point of intersection; the line of intersection of two planes; the perpendicular distance from a point to a plane; problems combining lines and planes.

concepts.name: First-order differential equations with separable variables
concepts.description: ZIMSEC Pure (F6) and Cambridge P3 (A Level only), topic 3.8. Writing a statement about a rate of change as a differential equation (with a constant of proportionality); finding the general solution by separating the variables and integrating (any technique of the family); a particular solution from an initial condition; interpreting the solution in the context modelled (growth, cooling, draining tanks). ZIMSEC only: sketching members of the family of solution curves.

concepts.name: Complex numbers in Cartesian form
concepts.description: ZIMSEC Pure (F5) and Cambridge P3 (A Level only), topic 3.9. The idea of a complex number; real part, imaginary part, conjugate (z*); equality of complex numbers; addition, subtraction, multiplication and division of x + iy with full working; quadratic equations with complex roots; the two square roots of a complex number (such as 5 + 12i) in exact Cartesian form.

concepts.name: The Argand diagram, modulus–argument and polar form
concepts.description: ZIMSEC Pure (F5 Argand diagram, F6 polar form) and Cambridge P3 (A Level only). Representing complex numbers on an Argand diagram; modulus and argument (usually −π < θ ≤ π); the polar form r(cos θ + i sin θ) = re^(iθ); multiplication and division in polar form, |z₁z₂| = |z₁||z₂| and arg(z₁z₂) = arg z₁ + arg z₂; the geometric effect of conjugating, adding, subtracting, multiplying and dividing.

concepts.name: Polynomial equations with complex roots
concepts.description: ZIMSEC Pure (F6, equations up to degree 5) and Cambridge P3 (A Level only). Non-real roots of polynomials with real coefficients occur in conjugate pairs; solving cubic and quartic (ZIMSEC up to quintic) equations when one complex root is given or can be found; forming a polynomial from given roots.

concepts.name: Loci in the Argand diagram
concepts.description: ZIMSEC Pure (F6) and Cambridge P3 (A Level only). Illustrating equations and inequalities by loci: |z − a| = k and |z − a| < k (circles and discs), |z − a| = |z − b| (perpendicular bisectors), arg(z − a) = α (half-lines), and regions defined by several conditions; least and greatest values of |z| or arg z in a region.

concepts.name: De Moivre's theorem and nth roots
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only: ZIMSEC Pure (F6). De Moivre's theorem (derived and proved by induction for positive integers, extended to negative integers); powers of complex numbers; expressing cos nθ and sin nθ in powers of cos θ and sin θ and powers of sin θ and cos θ in multiple angles; solving zⁿ = w; the nth roots of unity and their geometry (regular polygon) and sum.

concepts.name: Data collection, types of data and statistical diagrams
concepts.description: ZIMSEC Statistics (F5) and Cambridge P5 (AS & A Level), topic 5.1. Selecting a suitable way to present raw data and discussing advantages and disadvantages; stem-and-leaf diagrams (including back-to-back) and box-and-whisker plots, drawn and interpreted. ZIMSEC only: methods of collecting data and designing instruments (questionnaires, interviews, observation, experiments, records), types of data (primary and secondary, qualitative and quantitative, discrete and continuous), and bar graphs, pie charts, pictograms and line graphs.

concepts.name: Histograms and cumulative frequency graphs
concepts.description: ZIMSEC Statistics (F5) and Cambridge P5 (AS & A Level). Histograms with equal and unequal class widths (class boundaries, frequency density); cumulative frequency graphs used to estimate the median, quartiles, percentiles, and the proportion of a distribution above, below or between given values. ZIMSEC also frequency polygons.

concepts.name: Measures of central tendency and spread
concepts.description: ZIMSEC Statistics (F5) and Cambridge P5 (AS & A Level). Mean, median and mode of raw, ungrouped and grouped data; range, quartiles, interquartile range and percentiles; choosing a measure; comparing and contrasting data sets with a measure of location and a measure of spread.

concepts.name: Mean and standard deviation, including summary and coded data
concepts.description: ZIMSEC Statistics (F5) and Cambridge P5 (AS & A Level). Variance and standard deviation of raw, frequency and grouped data; using totals Σx and Σx² and coded totals Σ(x − a) and Σ(x − a)²; combining two data sets; solving problems with up to two data sets.

concepts.name: Permutations: arrangements in a line
concepts.description: ZIMSEC Statistics (F5) and Cambridge P5 (AS & A Level), topic 5.2. n!, nPr and the meaning of a permutation; arrangements of objects in a line with repetition (the letters of NEEDLESS) and restrictions (two people together or apart, items at the ends), people in two or more rows. Arrangements in a circle are excluded (Cambridge).

concepts.name: Combinations: selections
concepts.description: ZIMSEC Statistics (F5) and Cambridge P5 (AS & A Level). nCr and the meaning of a combination; selections with conditions (at least, at most, particular items included or excluded, from several groups); problems needing both selections and arrangements.

concepts.name: Probability: sample spaces, events and the addition rule
concepts.description: ZIMSEC Statistics (F5, F6) and Cambridge P5 (AS & A Level), topic 5.3. Probability key terms; enumerating equiprobable outcomes (total score of two dice, balls from a bag); probabilities using permutations and combinations; mutually exclusive, exhaustive and combined events; Venn diagrams and outcome tables; adding probabilities. The general rule P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A ∩ B) is used by ZIMSEC; Cambridge does not require it explicitly.

concepts.name: Conditional probability, independence and tree diagrams
concepts.description: ZIMSEC Statistics (F5, F6) and Cambridge P5 (AS & A Level). The multiplication of probabilities, tree diagrams with and without replacement, conditional probability P(A | B) = P(A ∩ B)/P(B) in simple cases (including contexts with permutations and combinations), and testing independence by comparing P(A ∩ B) with P(A) × P(B).

concepts.name: Bayes' theorem
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only: ZIMSEC Statistics (F6). Statement of Bayes' theorem for a partition of two or more events, its justification from the definition of conditional probability, and its use to reverse a conditional probability (medical tests, factory machines, weather forecasts) with tree diagrams.

concepts.name: Discrete random variables: expectation and variance
concepts.description: ZIMSEC Statistics (F5) and Cambridge P5 (AS & A Level), topic 5.4. Random variables; drawing up a probability distribution table for a situation; ΣP = 1 and unknown probabilities; E(X), Var(X) and standard deviation. ZIMSEC only: the discrete uniform distribution and its mean and variance.

concepts.name: The binomial distribution
concepts.description: ZIMSEC Statistics (F5) and Cambridge P5 (AS & A Level). Conditions for a binomial model, B(n, p), probabilities from the formula (exactly, at most, at least, between), mean np and variance np(1 − p), finding n or p, practical situations. ZIMSEC only (F6): the Bernoulli distribution with mean p and variance p(1 − p).

concepts.name: The geometric distribution
concepts.description: ZIMSEC Statistics (F5) and Cambridge P5 (AS & A Level). Geo(p) with P(X = r) = p(1 − p)^(r−1) for r = 1, 2, 3, …, P(X > r) = (1 − p)^r, suitable practical situations and the expectation 1/p. ZIMSEC also the variance (1 − p)/p² and standard deviation (Cambridge requires the expectation only).

concepts.name: The Poisson distribution
concepts.description: ZIMSEC Statistics (F6) and Cambridge P6 (A Level only), topic 6.1. Po(λ) probabilities from the formula; mean and variance both equal to λ; the relevance of the Poisson distribution to random events (independent, at a constant average rate) and its use as a model, scaling λ to the interval.

concepts.name: Poisson and normal approximations to the binomial and Poisson distributions
concepts.description: Cambridge only: Cambridge P6 (A Level only), topic 6.1. The Poisson approximation to the binomial distribution when n is large and p small (about n > 50 and np < 5) and the normal approximation to the Poisson distribution with a continuity correction when λ is large (about λ > 15). The normal approximation to the binomial is in amaths.normal.binomial-approximation.

concepts.name: The normal distribution: standardising and finding probabilities
concepts.description: ZIMSEC Statistics (F5) and Cambridge P5 (AS & A Level), topic 5.5. Properties of the normal curve and its use to model continuous variables; X ~ N(μ, σ²); standardising Z = (X − μ)/σ with full working; using normal tables (values computed in code here) to find P(X > x₁), P(X < x₁) and probabilities between values; sketches to illustrate.

concepts.name: The normal distribution: finding values, the mean and the standard deviation
concepts.description: ZIMSEC Statistics (F5) and Cambridge P5 (AS & A Level). Using the tables in reverse to find a value x₁ from a probability, and to find μ, σ or both (simultaneous equations) from given probabilities, in context.

concepts.name: The normal approximation to the binomial distribution
concepts.description: ZIMSEC Statistics (F5) and Cambridge P5 (AS & A Level). The conditions (n large enough that np > 5 and nq > 5), the parameters np and npq, the continuity correction, and using the approximation to solve problems; the normal distribution as a model.

concepts.name: Continuous random variables and probability density functions
concepts.description: ZIMSEC Statistics (F5) and Cambridge P6 (A Level only), topic 6.3. The concept of a continuous random variable; properties of a probability density function (non-negative, total area 1, defined over a single interval that may be infinite, e.g. 3/x⁴ for x ≥ 1); probabilities by integration; finding an unknown constant; mean, variance and standard deviation; the median and other percentiles by direct consideration of area. ZIMSEC also the mode. The cumulative distribution function is ZIMSEC only (amaths.continuous.cdf).

concepts.name: Cumulative distribution functions
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only: ZIMSEC Statistics (F5). The cumulative distribution function F(x) = P(X ≤ x) of a continuous random variable, finding F from f by integration (including piecewise pdfs) and f from F by differentiation, and using F for probabilities, the median, quartiles and percentiles.

concepts.name: The rectangular and exponential distributions
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only: ZIMSEC Statistics (rectangular F5, exponential F6). The continuous uniform (rectangular) distribution on [a, b] with mean (a + b)/2 and variance (b − a)²/12; the exponential distribution f(x) = λe^(−λx) for x ≥ 0, P(X > x) = e^(−λx), mean 1/λ and variance 1/λ² (derived with integration by parts), and problems on waiting times and lifetimes.

concepts.name: Linear combinations of random variables
concepts.description: ZIMSEC Statistics (F6) and Cambridge P6 (A Level only), topic 6.2. E(aX + b) = aE(X) + b and Var(aX + b) = a²Var(X); E(aX + bY) and Var(aX + bY) = a²Var(X) + b²Var(Y) for independent X and Y; aX + b and aX + bY are normal when X and Y are independent normals; the sum of independent Poisson variables is Poisson; the difference between 2X and X₁ + X₂. Proofs are not required.

concepts.name: Populations, samples and sampling methods
concepts.description: ZIMSEC Statistics (F5) and Cambridge P6 (A Level only), topic 6.4. Sample and population, the need for randomness, using random numbers to choose a random sample, and explaining why a given sampling method may be unsatisfactory (bias). ZIMSEC only: probability sampling techniques (simple random, systematic, stratified, cluster) and non-probability techniques (quota, convenience, judgement) with their uses, and choosing representative samples; Cambridge does not require particular methods.

concepts.name: The distribution of the sample mean and the central limit theorem
concepts.description: ZIMSEC Statistics (F6) and Cambridge P6 (A Level only). The sample mean X̄ as a random variable with E(X̄) = μ and Var(X̄) = σ²/n; X̄ is normal when X is normal; the central limit theorem (informally at Cambridge: for large n the sample mean is approximately normal) and its implications for small and large samples; probabilities about sample means and totals.

concepts.name: Unbiased estimates of the population mean and variance
concepts.description: ZIMSEC Statistics (F5) and Cambridge P6 (A Level only). Calculating unbiased estimates of the population mean and variance from raw data or from summaries (Σx, Σx², coded sums), the divisor n − 1, and a simple understanding of 'unbiased'; ZIMSEC also the sample mean, variance and standard deviation.

concepts.name: Confidence intervals for a mean and a proportion
concepts.description: ZIMSEC Statistics (F6) and Cambridge P6 (A Level only). Determining and interpreting a confidence interval for a population mean when the population is normal with known variance or when a large sample is used (σ estimated), and an approximate confidence interval for a population proportion from a large sample; widths and sample sizes. Intervals with the t-distribution (small samples, unknown variance) are ZIMSEC only (amaths.inference.t-distribution).

concepts.name: The language of hypothesis testing
concepts.description: ZIMSEC Statistics (F5) and Cambridge P6 (A Level only), topic 6.5. The nature of a hypothesis test; null and alternative hypotheses; one-tailed and two-tailed tests; significance level, test statistic, rejection (critical) region and acceptance region; formulating hypotheses and stating conclusions in context.

concepts.name: Hypothesis tests for a binomial proportion and a Poisson mean
concepts.description: ZIMSEC Statistics (F5: binomial) and Cambridge P6 (A Level only: binomial and Poisson). Tests based on a single observation from a binomial or Poisson distribution by direct evaluation of probabilities or by a normal approximation where appropriate; finding critical regions. Tests on a Poisson mean are Cambridge only.

concepts.name: Hypothesis tests for a population mean (z-tests)
concepts.description: ZIMSEC Statistics (F5) and Cambridge P6 (A Level only). Formulating hypotheses and testing a population mean with a sample from a normal distribution of known variance, or a large sample (z-test); critical values and comparison of probabilities; conclusions in context.

concepts.name: Type I and Type II errors
concepts.description: ZIMSEC Statistics (F5) and Cambridge P6 (A Level only). The meaning of Type I and Type II errors; calculating the probabilities of each in tests based on a normal distribution or on direct evaluation of binomial (and, Cambridge, Poisson) probabilities; the effect of changing the significance level.

concepts.name: The t-distribution: confidence intervals and t-tests
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only: ZIMSEC Statistics (F6). Characteristics of the t-distribution and degrees of freedom; confidence intervals for the mean of a normal population with unknown variance from a small sample (x̄ ± t s/√n); one-sample t-tests of a mean. Critical values are computed in code, not quoted from printed tables.

concepts.name: Chi-squared tests: goodness of fit and contingency tables
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only: ZIMSEC Statistics (F6). Characteristics of the χ² distribution and degrees of freedom; expected frequencies and combining classes with expected frequency below 5; goodness-of-fit tests (given ratios, uniform, binomial and Poisson models, with parameters estimated where needed) and tests for independence in contingency tables. Yates' correction is not named in the syllabus and is excluded.

concepts.name: Linear regression and correlation
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only: ZIMSEC Statistics (F6, Bivariate data). Scatter diagrams and lines of best fit; least-squares regression lines (y on x, and x on y) from data or summary statistics, prediction with interpolation and the risk of extrapolation; Pearson's product moment correlation coefficient r, its interpretation and the coefficient of determination r².

concepts.name: Time series: components, trends and moving averages
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only: ZIMSEC Statistics (F5, Time series). Time-series key terms and components (trend, seasonal, cyclical and irregular variation); time-series graphs; the purpose of smoothing; calculating and plotting moving averages (including centred averages for an even period); drawing trend lines and using them to identify and describe trends.

concepts.name: Forces, resultants and equilibrium of a particle
concepts.description: ZIMSEC Mechanics (F5) and Cambridge P4 (AS & A Level), topic 4.1. Identifying the forces in a situation with a force diagram (weight, normal reaction, tension, thrust, applied forces); the vector nature of force, components and resultants by calculation (never by scale drawing); equilibrium of a particle: the vector sum is zero, so components in any direction sum to zero (resolving; triangle of forces and Lami's theorem accepted but not required).

concepts.name: Friction and limiting equilibrium
concepts.description: ZIMSEC Mechanics (F5) and Cambridge P4 (AS & A Level). A contact force as a normal component and a frictional component; the smooth-contact model and its limitations; limiting friction and limiting equilibrium ('about to slip'), the coefficient of friction and F = μR or F ≤ μR; Newton's third law; particles on rough horizontal and inclined planes.

concepts.name: Moments and the equilibrium of a rigid body
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only: ZIMSEC Mechanics (F5, Vectors: moment of a force; Forces and equilibrium: rigid bodies). The moment of a force about a point (force × perpendicular distance, or from components), resultant moments, and equilibrium of a rigid body under coplanar forces (resultant force zero and total moment zero): beams on supports, hinged rods, ladders against walls with friction, bodies about to tilt. Cambridge 9709 treats every body as a particle.

concepts.name: Displacement–time and velocity–time graphs
concepts.description: ZIMSEC Mechanics (F5) and Cambridge P4 (AS & A Level), topic 4.2. Distance and speed as scalars, displacement, velocity and acceleration as vectors (one dimension); sketching and interpreting displacement–time and velocity–time graphs (area = displacement, gradients = velocity and acceleration); multi-stage journeys and 'deceleration'. ZIMSEC also distance–time and acceleration–time graphs.

concepts.name: Motion in a straight line with constant acceleration
concepts.description: ZIMSEC Mechanics (F5) and Cambridge P4 (AS & A Level). The constant-acceleration formulae (derived for ZIMSEC) and their use, including vertical motion under gravity, motion at constant velocity, and problems with two particles needing more than one equation. Cambridge uses g = 10 m s⁻²; ZIMSEC items state g.

concepts.name: Kinematics using calculus
concepts.description: ZIMSEC Mechanics (F5) and Cambridge P4 (AS & A Level). v = ds/dt, a = dv/dt and integration with respect to time with initial conditions, for motion with variable acceleration given as a function of time (Cambridge: calculus of P1 only, so powers of t); when a particle is at rest, maximum velocity, distance travelled when the direction changes.

concepts.name: Vectors in kinematics: positions, velocities and paths
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only: ZIMSEC Mechanics (F5, Vectors). The vector equation of a line and of the path of a particle moving with constant velocity (r = r₀ + tv); speed and direction of motion; whether two particles collide or their paths cross; the position vector of the point of intersection of two lines or paths. Cambridge 9709 does not use vector notation in Mechanics.

concepts.name: Newton's laws of motion: F = ma, weight and inclined planes
concepts.description: ZIMSEC Mechanics (F5) and Cambridge P4 (AS & A Level), topic 4.4. Newton's three laws; F = ma for a particle of constant mass under constant forces (friction, tension, thrust, resistances stated in the question); mass and weight W = mg; vertical motion (lifts) and motion caused by several forces (resolving); motion on smooth and rough inclined planes, where the acceleration up the plane differs from that down it.

concepts.name: Connected particles: strings, pulleys and tow-bars
concepts.description: ZIMSEC Mechanics (F5) and Cambridge P4 (AS & A Level). Two particles connected by a light inextensible string over a fixed smooth light pulley or peg (hanging, or one on a horizontal or inclined plane); a car towing a trailer by a light rope or a light rigid tow-bar (tension or thrust); what happens when a string becomes slack or a particle reaches the pulley or the ground.

concepts.name: Momentum, impulse and collisions
concepts.description: ZIMSEC Mechanics (F5) and Cambridge P4 (AS & A Level), topic 4.3. Linear momentum and its vector nature (one dimension); conservation of linear momentum in direct impacts of two bodies, including bodies that coalesce. ZIMSEC only: impulse as force × time and as change of momentum, impulsive forces (including jerks in strings). Coefficient of restitution is excluded.

concepts.name: Work, energy and the work–energy principle
concepts.description: ZIMSEC Mechanics (F6) and Cambridge P4 (AS & A Level), topic 4.5. Work done by a constant force (W = Fd cos θ, without scalar products); kinetic and gravitational potential energy; the change in energy of a system and the work done by external forces (work against resistance and friction); conservation of energy, including non-linear paths (a smooth curved slide) where only overall energy changes matter. Elastic potential energy is in amaths.elasticity.hookes-law-energy.

concepts.name: Power
concepts.description: ZIMSEC Mechanics (F6) and Cambridge P4 (AS & A Level). Power as the rate at which a force does work, average power = work done ÷ time, P = Fv for a force in the direction of motion; maximum speed, and the instantaneous acceleration of a vehicle on a level road or a hill against a resistance.

concepts.name: Projectiles
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only: ZIMSEC Mechanics (F5, Motion of a projectile). A projectile as a particle with constant acceleration g; horizontal and vertical equations of motion; position and the magnitude and direction of velocity at a given time; time of flight, range on a horizontal plane and greatest height, with the general formulae derived; the maximum range; the Cartesian equation of the trajectory and its use (for example the two angles of projection that reach a given point).

concepts.name: Centre of mass: uniform bodies, composite laminas, suspension and toppling
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only: ZIMSEC Mechanics (F6, Centre of mass). Centre of gravity and centre of mass; systems of particles; standard positions for a uniform rod, circular hoop, rectangular and circular laminas, triangular lamina, solid and hollow cylinders and spheres; composite laminas and laminas with parts removed; a body suspended freely from a point (angle with the vertical); whether a body on an inclined plane slides or topples first.

concepts.name: Elastic strings and springs: Hooke's law and elastic energy
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only: ZIMSEC Mechanics (F6, Elasticity). Properties of light elastic strings and springs; Hooke's law T = λx/l and the modulus of elasticity; equilibrium problems; work done in stretching a string and elastic potential energy λx²/(2l); conservation of mechanical energy with elastic strings and springs (bungee jumps, catapults).

concepts.name: Motion in a circle
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only: ZIMSEC Mechanics (F6, Circular motion). Angular speed and velocity, v = rω, acceleration rω² = v²/r towards the centre for a particle moving in a circle with constant speed; horizontal circles (particle on a turntable or a string, conical pendulum: tension and angular speed, banked tracks); vertical circles (the syllabus names vertical circular motion 'with constant speed'; energy methods for varying speed to be confirmed by the reviewer).

concepts.name: Linear motion under a variable force
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only: ZIMSEC Mechanics (F6). Acceleration as a function of time, displacement (a = v dv/dx) or velocity; Newton's second law with a variable force (resistances proportional to v or v²) set up and solved as first-order separable differential equations; displacement as a function of time and velocity as a function of displacement; variable motion in the x–y plane with position, velocity and acceleration vectors.

concepts.name: Simple harmonic motion
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only: ZIMSEC Mechanics (F6). The definition ẍ = −ω²x; standard results x = a sin(ωt + ε), v² = ω²(a² − x²), period 2π/ω, amplitude, maximum speed and acceleration; forming the differential equation from the forces (particles on elastic strings or springs, the simple pendulum for small oscillations with period 2π√(l/g)) and solving it for period and amplitude.
